display.purpose: The landing hero and marketing-page openers. One per screen.

headline.purpose: Section openers on every long-form surface.

label.purpose: The stamp utility: column headers and small uppercase markers. Identifiers only, never money.

amount.purpose: The figure being entered or committed. Outranks the heading above it.

body-sm.purpose: The interface workhorse: row labels, secondary lines, sentences inside cards.

body-ui.purpose: Interface prose: button labels, list rows, sheet lines.

figure-lg.purpose: The one number a screen exists to show: portfolio value, cash, borrowing power.

figure.purpose: A secondary headline number, such as a stock price.

moment-title.purpose: The heading of a dialog marking an occasion: welcome, account ready.

page-title.purpose: The heading of an app screen or a task sheet.

lead.purpose: The paragraph directly under a display heading. One per surface.

code.purpose: The one-time-code field's digits, sized so a six-character code reads as six objects rather than a word.

shadows.name: seated
shadows.purpose: The sheet rests on the one below it. Active sidebar item, small pills.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Hover on a card that can be picked up.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Dropdown or popover held above the page.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Modals and sheets only, where the sheet genuinely is off the desk.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Confident deceleration. Default easing for every transition and entrance.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Press and hover feedback, fast enough to read as cause and effect.

motion.name: mark
motion.purpose: A logo or mark reacting to the pointer.

motion.name: card-in
motion.purpose: Cards arrive with more travel because they carry more weight.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: movement removed; colour and opacity transitions kept at 120ms
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion an action still acknowledges itself.

narrative.overview:
Harbor is set, not styled. The ground is warm off-white paper rather than white or dark; structure comes from hairline rules and the edges of sheets, not from boxes with shadows; and every figure sits in a tabular column so that columns of money actually line up. Authority is meant to come from typesetting the way it does on a bank statement or a prospectus, where nothing is decorated and nothing needs to be.

The density is deliberately unhurried. A screen carries one idea, states it in a heading, supports it with one paragraph at reading measure, and then shows the numbers. Colour is scarce: a single teal appears only where something is actionable or live, and the gain/loss pair appears only on figures that actually moved. Most of any screen is paper, ink and rules.

Restraint here is a trust argument, not a taste preference. This is a product that refuses orders, queues them, and tells people they can be sold out of a position while they sleep — the interface has to feel like it is reading from a record rather than selling something.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground (Statement Paper #efede8), never white and never dark
Hairline rules carry structure; borders replace shadows
Harbour Teal on under a tenth of any screen, only where something is actionable or live
Tabular numerals globally, so figures align down a column
Monospace reserved for identifiers, never for prose or money
Every number says where it came from

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Harbour Teal appears on at most a tenth of any screen. If a second thing wants to be teal, one of them is not actually actionable.

rules.name: The Earned Colour Rule
rules.body: Gain, Loss and Caution are applied to figures and verdicts that genuinely moved or genuinely changed state. A number that is merely important stays Ink.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor
rules.body: Every text colour clears 4.5:1 on every ground it is permitted to sit on. Faint is #6f6a60 rather than something lighter for exactly this reason. Sustained prose on Statement Paper uses Muted, not Faint.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Identifiers Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for tickers, token symbols, wallet addresses, mint addresses, multipliers, route labels and stamp labels. It is never used for dollar figures, share counts, percentages, or prose.

rules.name: The Aligned Figures Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set globally on body. Every column of money lines up by default, and nothing should opt out.

rules.name: The Tightening Rule
rules.body: Letter-spacing tightens as type grows (-0.01em at title, -0.035em at display) and never goes positive except on the 11px uppercase stamp, where it opens to 0.1em.

rules.name: The Restructure Don't Shrink Rule
rules.body: When a horizontal row cannot hold its columns, it becomes stacked lines with the same information. Nothing is truncated to fit and no font size drops below its step to buy width.

rules.name: The Hairline Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs separating, give it a border. Reach for a shadow only when the surface is genuinely above the page — hovered, dragged, or modal.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: A container inside a card steps down one level (16px outer, 14px inner). Two identical radii nested inside each other read as a mistake.

rules.name: The One Step-Up Rule
rules.body: A role that grows at a breakpoint grows to exactly one documented value. Section headings that step to 36 in one file, 38 in another and 40 in four more are not a scale, they are an accident. The same holds for dialog titles: one step-up value, not two.

dos: Do put every app screen on Statement Paper (#efede8) and reserve white for cards.
Do separate surfaces with a hairline before reaching for a shadow.
Do keep Harbour Teal under a tenth of the screen, on things that are actionable or live.
Do use JetBrains Mono for tickers, addresses, multipliers and route labels only.
Do state a figure's source next to it, because provenance is part of this product's visual language.
Do restructure rows into stacked lines on narrow screens rather than shrinking type.
Do step a nested container's radius down one level from its parent.
Do hold every screen to WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44px targets under coarse pointers.
donts: Don't reach for the fintech startup template: purple-to-blue gradients on white, oversized rounded cards, 3D illustrated mascots, or a hero with a floating phone mock. This is the one named anti-reference.
Don't set a kicker or eyebrow above a heading. The heading carries its own weight.
Don't put a monospace face on a dollar figure, a share count or a percentage.
Don't give a component a shadow at rest.
Don't use Faint for sustained prose on Statement Paper; that is Muted's job.
Don't colour a figure green or red unless it actually moved, or amber unless it is genuinely in a third state.
Don't draw a bar, ring or sparkline to stand in for content that could be stated as aligned text and read exactly.
Don't nest a card inside a card.
